correctness.rationale: For binary x, strict majority flip at every vertex of F gives sum_F(2b_v-deg(v))>=|F|. Counting edges leaving and inside F yields J(y)-J(x)=a-b<=2c-|F|<=c-c(F)<=J(x)-c(F), using the induced forest size |F|-c(F). With J(x)=k integer, also J(y)<=n-1; maximization of min(2-1/k,(n-1)/k) yields 2-1/floor(n/2). Odd-sized median commutes with thresholds, and graph coarea transfers the bound to arbitrary real f. A star on 2q vertices and a once-subdivided star on 2q+1 vertices attain it; n=2,3 have gain one. Independent all labeled trees n=2..5 and every nonconstant binary input (145 trees; 3994 signals) independently confirmed the component deficit and bound.
residual_risks: No exact gain classification for individual trees, weighted graphs, asynchronous or distinct median neighborhoods; binary finite tests do not establish real/all-n theorem alone.
